subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add a broad execution-enforcement guard system for artifact-gated status updates, persisted run state, escalation timers, and post-green idle handling, or should maintainers keep improving the existing narrower loop/session diagnostics?
rationale: The request is useful but broad: it adds enforcement policy, persistence, telemetry, timer thresholds, and a new flag across core agent/session behavior, so automation should not choose the product shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design Narrow Core Guards
options.body: Approve a scoped design that extends existing loop detection and session-liveness paths without adding a parallel orchestration layer.

options.title: Defer To Existing Diagnostics
options.body: Keep current tool-loop and session-stall guardrails, and only tune them when concrete repros show remaining gaps.

options.title: Split Smaller Trackers
options.body: Close or supersede this umbrella only after creating narrower canonical issues for status gating, persistence, timers, and post-green behavior.

recommendation.title: Design Narrow Core Guards
recommendation.body: Approve a scoped design that extends existing loop detection and session-liveness paths without adding a parallel orchestration layer.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing owner from the inspected history because they merged the recent guard-related boundary commit and can redirect the product decision to the right area owner.
